assumptions: gh-flaky follows the CLI-wide gate contract (0 verified zero, 1 candidates, 3 abstained or unverifiable), unlike the history-backed analyze subcommands, which stay advisory at exit 0.
A gh row missing a numeric databaseId or a string headSha is skipped but counted as skippedRows and disclosed in the text output, so the checked-run denominator cannot shrink silently.
A rerun is inspected only when its current conclusion is success; a rerun still red is already a visible failure and not a hidden flake.

Only completed outcomes take part: a conclusion of "" (in progress), null, skipped, neutral, action_required or stale is a non-outcome. Non-outcome runs and earlier attempts are never a flip partner or rerun candidate; they are counted as nonOutcomeRows and disclosed in text and JSON notes.
A completed non-success earlier attempt (failure, cancelled, timed_out, startup_failure) counts as a rerun-attempt candidate.
A same-SHA flip is a sha + workflow group whose completed outcomes include success and at least one failure-class conclusion.

A row with no numeric attempt is never defaulted to 1: it is counted as missingAttemptRows, rerun-attempt is dropped from verifiedAgainst, and a window with no candidates is flake-signal-unverifiable (exit 3), with the cause named in text and JSON notes.
--repo is required rather than inferred from the working directory, matching batwoman's gh seam.

The window is the last --limit-runs runs (default 100) across all workflows. A page that fills to the limit is reported as truncated (complete: false, 'window truncated at N runs; older runs unchecked') in both text and --json output; the verdict and exit code still cover the declared window, so truncation is disclosed, not abstained on.
Perf paydown is the commonFailuresCmd row-building loop in ts/src/analysis/cli.ts, which decides no gate verdict and is not one of #904-#907.
